gen-gf-hi-melody-fs-plein: Hand-drawn letters huddled close, like tiles pressed together. Plein, a sans-serif, gives each round letter a clear channel in, and a modest body size keeps it pleasant to read in bursts.
gen-gf-hi-melody-fs-synonym: Synonym sets down a plain stripe of constant ink, every curve generously open. Synonym stays orderly beside Hi Melody, whose hand-drawn letters huddle like tiles, though it wants brevity, not endless pages.
gen-gf-iansui-fs-synonym: Synonym lays down a plain stripe of constant ink. Iansui's flared, hand-drawn curve ends set friendly handwriting against precise geometry, a pairing best kept brief rather than stretched over pages.
gen-gf-iansui-outfit: Iansui writes with a friendly, hand-drawn looseness. Outfit bends its strokes like cable, curves stopping short of closing, so beneath that loose hand the text stays tidy but brief.
gen-gf-iansui-sora: Sora draws its curves with no pressure swell at the corners. Iansui's flared, hand-drawn curve ends set friendly handwriting against precise geometry, a pairing best kept brief rather than stretched over pages.
gen-gf-iceland-fs-rowan: Solid blocks of words, cut at a single engraved depth. Rowan lets thin strokes run about half the weight of thick ones, so it feels alive beside Iceland, though it prefers brief lines.
gen-gf-itim-archivo: Itim writes casually, its ascenders rising only a short stretch above the midline. And Archivo opens its curves outward under a commanding x-height, which keeps text friendly for brief reading but would tire across many pages.
gen-gf-itim-fs-fira-sans: Itim scrawls casual, friendly letters with a short climb from midline to ascender, giving the heading a loose handwritten ease. Fira Sans holds one steady line, with an ample x-height, for brief text.
gen-gf-itim-fs-public-sans: Casual and friendly, Itim writes with a short climb from midline to ascender. But Public Sans brings a hefty lowercase with broad open counters, so it suits brief text, not page after page.
gen-gf-itim-fs-supreme: Supreme reads crisp and heavy, a thick strip of text through the middle, with letters held open rather than curled shut. Itim adds casual handwriting up top, though pages of Supreme would feel dense.
